title: Central additive series of a smooth connected unipotent group over a perfect field
statement:
Let $k$ be a perfect field [def-weil-field], meaning that every algebraic extension of $k$ is separable. Let $U$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume that $U$ is unipotent: in a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation, every point over an algebraically closed extension of $k$ has nilpotent difference from the identity matrix. There exist an integer $m\geq0$ and smooth connected closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]
$$U=U_0\supseteq U_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq U_m=1$$
such that every $U_j$ is normal in $U$, every represented fppf group-sheaf quotient $U_j/U_{j+1}$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{a,k}$ [def-sc-gm-ga], and $U_j/U_{j+1}$ is central in $U/U_{j+1}$. Central means that all its sections commute with all sections of $U/U_{j+1}$ after every base change. Here $1=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the trivial group; fppf quotients are sheafifications of the orbit presheaves for faithfully flat finitely presented covers [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The trivial group admits the series with $m=0$.

source.place: Corollary 16.24, printed p.331, first assertion (central normal series with additive quotients); Corollary 16.23 and Corollary 16.22, printed p.331, supply its induction.

proof.text: The underlying scheme of $\mathbf G_a$ is $\mathbf A^1_k$ by [def-sc-gm-ga]. It is nonempty (the identity is a point), smooth of relative dimension $1$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], and therefore has Krull dimension $1$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-fixed-dimension-over-field]. An affine group is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. The finiteness assertion in [lem-sfb-homogeneous-quotient-krull-dimension], applied to any such group $V$ and its trivial subgroup (whose coset quotient is $V$ with the identity map), makes $\dim V$ a finite nonnegative integer. We prove the assertion for every smooth connected affine unipotent finite-type $k$-group scheme $V$ over the fixed perfect field by strong induction on this integer. If $V=1$, take $m=0$; there are no quotient or centrality conditions to check.

source.place: Corollary 16.24, printed p.331, induction from Corollary 16.23; dimensions by Proposition 5.23, printed p.104.

proof.text: Suppose $V\ne1$. Apply [lem-sfb-unipotent-central-additive-subgroup] to obtain a smooth connected central closed subgroup $N\subseteq V$ with $N\cong\mathbf G_a$. Its perfectness convention follows from ours: in characteristic $p$, a root of $T^p-a$ generates a purely inseparable algebraic extension, which must be separable and hence trivial, so every $a\in k$ is a $p$-th power. Centrality implies normality on every test algebra. By [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected], the identity point makes $V$ geometrically connected. Now [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] supplies $q:V\to Q=V/N$, affine of finite type, smooth and geometrically connected, with kernel $N$; $q$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented. In particular $Q$ is connected.

source.place: Corollary 16.24, printed p.331, induction from Corollary 16.23; dimensions by Proposition 5.23, printed p.104.

proof.text: We verify the remaining induction hypothesis, unipotence of $Q$, without assuming that $k$ is algebraically closed. The field-extension clause of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] identifies $q_{\bar k}$ with $V_{\bar k}\to V_{\bar k}/N_{\bar k}$. In [lem-sfb-unipotent-normal-quotient-image], take $A=V_{\bar k}$, $D=I=Q_{\bar k}$, the node's normal subgroup equal to all of $A$, $f=u=q_{\bar k}$ and $j=\mathrm{id}$. The source is smooth, connected and unipotent and $q_{\bar k}$ is faithfully flat, so that node gives unipotence of $Q_{\bar k}$. The field-extension detection and the smooth geometric-matrix criterion explicitly stated in [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial] give precisely unipotence of $Q$ in the geometric-matrix sense specified above. The coset quotient $V/N$ also satisfies the homogeneous-quotient hypothesis: its kernel identifies coset fibres and its fppf local lifts are fpqc local lifts. Thus [lem-sfb-homogeneous-quotient-krull-dimension] gives $\dim V=\dim N+\dim Q=1+\dim Q$. Hence $\dim Q<\dim V$. If $\dim V=0$, this is already a contradiction, settling the induction base.

source.place: Corollary 16.24, printed p.331, induction from Corollary 16.23; dimensions by Proposition 5.23, printed p.104.

proof.text: Apply the strong induction hypothesis to $Q$: write $Q=Q_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq Q_r=1$ with all terms smooth connected and normal in $Q$, and with central additive successive quotients. Set $P_i=q^{-1}(Q_i)$ for $0\le i\le r$. By [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry], these are closed subgroup schemes, smooth and connected since $N$ and $Q_i$ are so, normal in $V$, with $P_0=V$, $P_r=N$ and $P_i/P_{i+1}\cong Q_i/Q_{i+1}\cong\mathbf G_a$. The same correspondence identifies $V/P_{i+1}$ with $Q/Q_{i+1}$: apply its quotient clause to the pair $Q_{i+1}\triangleleft Q$ and their inverse images. Append $P_{r+1}=1$. The last quotient is $N/1=N\cong\mathbf G_a$. Thus $m=r+1$ and this chain has every required geometric and quotient property.

source.place: Corollary 16.24, printed p.331, induction from Corollary 16.23; dimensions by Proposition 5.23, printed p.104.

proof.text: For $i<r$, under $V/P_{i+1}\cong Q/Q_{i+1}$ the subgroup $P_i/P_{i+1}$ is exactly $Q_i/Q_{i+1}$. On any test scheme, and after any further base change, the latter commutes with every section of $Q/Q_{i+1}$ by the induction hypothesis. The isomorphisms preserve products, so the former commutes with every section of $V/P_{i+1}$. For $i=r$, this is the centrality of $N$ in $V$ chosen in step 2. The appended trivial subgroup is normal, smooth and connected. This proves the centrality clauses and completes the induction, including $Q=1$ (then $r=0$ and the chain is $V=N\supseteq1$).
